name: Ivy League haircut

lead: The Ivy League is a type of crew cut in which the top is left long enough to part at the side while the crown and the sides and back are cut short. It gives a tidy, collegiate look that is easy to style and works with a suit or casual clothes.
It dates to at least the 1950s and is also called the Harvard clip or Princeton.

paras: The barber tapers the sides and back and leaves length on top; it can be side-parted, brushed up into a short pompadour or worn forward, usually with a light wax. Regular trims keep the shape.
No health risks; the main limitation is that a short cut shows head shape and hairline, and thinning hair may show.

chain: Short tapered sides with a longer top
Clean, classic frame for the face
angle.text: The cut keeps hair short and tidy while allowing a side part or short pompadour, giving a clean-cut look with flexible styling.

lead: The Ivy League haircut, also called the Harvard clip or Princeton, is a type of crew cut with enough length on top to part at the side. People choose it for a neat, classic look that is low-maintenance. [1]

Wikipedia describes the sides and back as tapered short, semi-short or medium, with length varying by skull shape and hair type. It can be worn side-parted, brushed up in a short pompadour, or as a standard crew cut, traditionally with butch wax. [1] Sources it cites date the style to the 1950s, including a 1959 Time article. [1]
It is called a convertible haircut because it can be styled several ways. [1]

paras: It is a subtype of the crew cut distinguished by a longer, side-parted top, and similar to a forward brush, which is styled forward. [1]

timeline.event: The style appears in 1950s sources such as a 1955 Cornell crew photo and a 1959 Time article. [1]
